title: Student Privacy & Campus Surveillance Security Checklist
metaDescription: Essential checklist to protect your student data and understand campus surveillance systems. Safeguard your educational privacy rights.
intro: Modern campuses use extensive surveillance and data collection systems that can impact your privacy. This checklist helps you understand your rights, protect your personal information, and navigate campus monitoring systems safely.

items.why: FERPA gives you control over who can access your educational records and how they're shared.
items.howTo: Contact your school's registrar office for FERPA information. Request a copy of your rights documentation and understand what data the school collects about you.

items.task: Audit what data your school collects
items.why: Schools collect extensive data beyond grades, including behavioral, biometric, and digital activity data.
items.howTo: Review your student handbook and privacy policies. Ask administrators what data is collected through campus cards, WiFi, learning management systems, and surveillance cameras.

items.why: Many data collection practices have opt-out provisions that aren't clearly communicated to students.
items.howTo: Check for directory information opt-outs, marketing communications preferences, and optional data sharing programs. Submit opt-out requests in writing.

items.why: Understanding camera locations helps you make informed decisions about where to have private conversations.
items.howTo: Walk around campus and note camera locations. Check with campus security about surveillance policies and data retention periods.

items.why: Campus networks often monitor and log all internet activity, creating detailed profiles of student behavior.
items.howTo: Read the campus IT acceptable use policy. Use Incognito Browser and consider a VPN for sensitive browsing. Use personal mobile data for private activities.

items.why: Student ID cards create detailed logs of your campus movements and purchasing habits.
items.howTo: Ask about data retention policies for card swipes. Understand what information is shared and with whom. Consider using cash for purchases when possible.

items.why: Learning platforms track detailed data about your study habits, performance, and engagement patterns.
items.howTo: Review privacy settings in Canvas, Blackboard, or other platforms. Limit profile visibility and understand what data is shared with instructors and third parties.

items.why: Proctoring software can access your camera, microphone, screen, and personal files during exams.
items.howTo: Read proctoring software privacy policies. Use a dedicated computer or create a separate user account for exams. Cover cameras when not in use.

items.why: Academic research topics can be sensitive and monitoring can create chilling effects on intellectual freedom.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser for sensitive research topics. Clear browsing data regularly. Consider using library computers for particularly sensitive research.

items.why: Student emails are subject to monitoring and can be accessed by administrators under certain circumstances.
items.howTo: Enable two-factor authentication on your student email. Use personal email for sensitive communications. Understand your school's email monitoring policies.

items.why: Schools increasingly monitor student social media accounts, which can impact disciplinary actions and opportunities.
items.howTo: Review privacy settings on all social platforms. Avoid posting content that could be interpreted as violating school policies. Consider separate academic and personal accounts.

items.why: Educational apps often have broad data collection practices and may share information with multiple parties.
items.howTo: Check permissions for apps required by your courses. Read privacy policies for educational tools. Revoke unnecessary permissions and delete unused educational apps.
